subject.title: Feature: Native Audio Input for Omni-Modal Models (skip STT transcription)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in native audio model input for inbound channel audio, and what typed media, provider-egress, fallback, and transcript/audit contract should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent solution changes model content types, provider routing, raw voice egress, user config, fallback behavior, and session semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit opt-in egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before accepting implementation.

options.title: Keep inbound audio STT-only for now
options.body: Continue routing voice notes through tools.media.audio transcription until maintainers decide raw-media egress and session semantics are acceptable.

options.title: Narrow through the existing implementation PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78797 only after it is rebased, proves real behavior, and aligns with the approved native media contract.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit opt-in egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current media-understanding introduction, extracted contracts, and adjacent provider/media history point to steipete as the best available routing owner for the product contract decision.
